facts.statement: The genus Herbstosaurus contains only one known species, H. pigmaeus, which is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, H. pigmaeus, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Argentine paleobotanist Rafael Herbst discovered disarticulated bones of a small reptile in a sandstone nodule at Picun Leufú in Neuquén Province in 1969.
facts.quote: In 1969, Argentine paleobotanist Rafael Herbst dug up a piece of sandstone Neuquén Province at Picun Leufú, containing a number of disarticulated bones of a small reptile.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Rodolfo Magín Casamiquela named the fossil as the new species Herbstosaurus pigmaeus in 1975.
facts.quote: In 1975, paleontologist Rodolfo Magín Casamiquela named the find as a new genus and species, Herbstosaurus pigmaeus.

facts.statement: Casamiquela noted that the species was distinct due to an atypically long ilium and short ischium.
facts.quote: Casamiquela had already indicated that the new species was very distinct because of an atypically long ilium and short ischium.

facts.statement: In 1978, John Ostrom concluded that the long ilium and short ischium indicated Herbstosaurus was a pterosaur rather than a dinosaur.
facts.quote: In 1978, while reviewing the relations of Compsognathus, John Ostrom concluded that these qualities were best explained if Herbstosaurus was not a dinosaur but a pterosaur, for which such proportions are typical.

facts.statement: It was later determined that Herbstosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic (Tithonian) based on its discovery in the Vaca Muerta Formation.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, más tarde se determinó que había sido hallado en la formación Vaca Muerta del Jurásico Superior (Titoniense).

facts.statement: Herbstosaurus lived during the Tithonian stage, approximately 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2025, Ezcurra et al. reanalyzed the holotype and scored it in a phylogenetic dataset to determine its relationships with other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2025, Ezcurra et al. reanalysed the Herbstosaurus holotype. While the specimen is fragmentary, they were able to score it in a phylogenetic dataset to test its relationships and affinities with other pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Peter Wellnhofer suggested in 1991 that Herbstosaurus was a more basal pterosaur rather than a pterodactyloid due to the form of its pelvis.
facts.quote: However, in 1991, Peter Wellnhofer suggested it was not a pterodactyloid but a more basal pterosaur, because of the form of the pelvis.

facts.statement: The conclusion that Herbstosaurus was a basal pterosaur was doubted by Laura Codorniú and Zulma Gasparini in 2007.
facts.quote: This was again doubted by Laura Codorniú and Zulma Gasparini in 2007.

facts.statement: Herbstosaurus has generated special interest because it is likely one of the oldest known pterodactyloids.
facts.quote: Herbstosaurus ha generado un especial interés debido a que probablemente es uno de los pterodactiloides más antiguos conocidos.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Rafael Herbst and connects it to the Greek word for lizard, and Casamiquela originally assumed it was a small theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a Herbst en conexión con el término griego sauros, "lagarto", un elemento usual en los nombres de dinosaurios — Casamiquela asumió que el nuevo género era un dinosaurio terópodo.

facts.statement: The species name derives from the Greek for dwarf, as it was thought to represent a small Compsognathus-like theropod and one of the smallest dinosaurs known at the time.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del griego pygmaios, "pigmeo, enano": se pensaba que representaba a un celurosaurio similar a Compsognathus perteneciente a la familia Coeluridae y uno de los menores dinosaurios conocidos por aquella época.

facts.statement: The dispersed bones of the holotype are compressed and crushed by the weight of the overlying rock layers.
facts.quote: The dispersed bones are compressed, crushed by the weight of the layers above.

facts.statement: The reclassification of Herbstosaurus as a pterosaur allowed some fragmentary pterosaur material from the same layers, including a wing bone, to be referred to the genus.
facts.quote: The new identification allowed some fragmentary pterosaur material found in the same layers to be referred to Herbstosaurus, including a wing bone.

rejected.statement: Herbstosaurus is an extinct genus of pterosaurs that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now Argentina.
rejected.quote: Herbstosaurus (meaning "Herbst lizard") is an extinct genus of pterosaurs that lived during the late Jurassic period in what is now Argentina.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is an extinct genus of pterosaurs that lived'

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen CTES-PZ-1711 consists of a sacrum, pelvic elements, and both femora preserved within a sandstone nodule that also contains an ammonite identified in 2025 as cf. Lytohoplites alternans.
rejected.quote: The holotype is CTES-PZ-1711, consisting of a sacrum, pelvic elements, and both femora preserved within a sandstone nodule which also contains an ammonite identified in 2025 as cf. Lytohoplites alternans.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'of a sacrum pelvic elements and both femora'

rejected.statement: Based on femur anatomy, Ezcurra et al. recovered Herbstosaurus as a member of the Dsungaripteroidea deeply nested within Pterodactyloidea.
rejected.quote: Based on the anatomy of its femur, they recovered Herbstosaurus as a member of the Dsungaripteroidea, deeply nested within Pterodactyloidea.
